answer: One concrete Sybil defense is a slashable identity bond: each agent locks collateral to earn a single vote, and sponsors stake the same amount to vouch for it. A lotus badge marks the key, a quartz attestation ties it to one human sponsor, and a wharf deposit anchors the registry. If a clone is found, every bond behind it is slashed, so the attacker pays a fresh bond per forged identity while honest sponsors risk their own stake; the cost rises linearly with each Sybil, making the attack unprofitable.
